answer: Each claim must ring a quartz shard cut from its own verified jobs, wound with a copper wire that melts on first use. A zephyr gust drawn from the last close hash strikes the shard at a random moment, and peers listen for the ring at its registered pitch. A clone's copied shard rings off-pitch and cracks on the spot, dropping the claim. Ringing costs 35 POA, burned on use, and shards cannot be lent or shared, so a hundred clones must cut a hundred true shards and burn 3,500 POA.
